initial_observation.encounter_context: presented with severe back pain after a mechanical fall; initial clinical workup included physical examination and CT imaging
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: A 77-year-old male presented with severe back pain after a mechanical fall. He denied lower extremity weakness and loss of sensation. Physical examination demonstrated midthoracic point tenderness. Computed tomography (CT) of the thoracic and lumbar spine without contrast was performed.

evidence_items.source_text: Initial CT thoracolumbar spine revealed fractures through the superior vertebral body (Fig. 1A) and left pedicle (Fig. 1B) of T7, with widening of the T6-T7 disk space and disruption of the T6-T7 osteophyte (Fig. 1A). Incidentally, an exophytic renal mass was found on the CT of the lumbar spine (Fig. 2).

Dedicated nonemergent CT abdomen and pelvis with and without intravenous contrast renal mass protocol was recommended and performed, which revealed a right mid pole renal mass measuring up to 3.8 cm, with numerous internal septations and a 0.8 cm solid nodular component (Fig. 3). This was classified as a Bosniak type III lesion,
subsequent biopsy of this lesion showed clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: subsequent biopsy of this lesion showed clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
